data.title: IRSF Traffic Spike Detection — Abnormal Call Volume to Premium-Rate International Numbers
data.description: Detects abnormal spikes in outbound call volume to premium-rate international number ranges, the hallmark indicator of International Revenue Share Fraud (IRSF). IRSF is the single largest telecom fraud category at $10.76B in annual losses (CFCA/TNS 2026). Fraudsters generate artificial traffic to premium-rate numbers where they hold revenue- sharing agreements, typically using compromised PBX systems or automated dialers. The detection uses z-score analysis against per-source baseline call volumes to premium-rate destinations, flagging when hourly volume exceeds 3 standard deviations. A compromised PBX can generate $50K-$500K in fraudulent charges within hours, making real-time detection critical.

enrichment_required.source: Premium-rate number range lookup table (CFCA/i3 Forum intelligence)
Country risk classification from telecom fraud intelligence
Rolling 30-day average hourly call volume per source to premium-rate destinations

queries.cql:
// CQL for IRSF Traffic Spike Detection — DL-0182
// Detects abnormal call volume to premium-rate international numbers using z-score
CallDetailRecords
| call_direction = "outbound"
| destination_type = "international"
| is_premium_rate = "true"
| groupBy([source_system, trunk_group, risk_country, hourly_bin],
    function=[count() as call_count,
              sum(call_duration_seconds) as total_duration_sec,
              countDistinct(calling_number) as unique_callers,
              countDistinct(called_number) as unique_destinations,
              avg(call_duration_seconds) as avg_duration])
| selfJoinFilter(key=[source_system, trunk_group],
    where=[avg(call_count) as baseline_count,
           stddev(call_count) as stdev_count])
| stdev_count > 0
| z_score := (call_count - baseline_count) / stdev_count
| z_score > 3
| sort(z_score, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for IRSF Traffic Spike Detection — DL-0182")`
`comment("Detects abnormal call volume to premium-rate international numbers")`
index=flame_telecom sourcetype=flame:cdr
  call_direction="outbound"
  destination_type="international"
| lookup premium_rate_ranges number_prefix OUTPUTNEW is_premium_rate, risk_country, per_minute_rate
| where is_premium_rate="true"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as call_count,
        sum(call_duration_seconds) as total_duration_sec,
        dc(calling_number) as unique_callers,
        dc(called_number) as unique_destinations,
        avg(call_duration_seconds) as avg_duration
  by source_system, trunk_group, risk_country, _time
| eventstats avg(call_count) as baseline_count, stdev(call_count) as stdev_count
  by source_system, trunk_group
| where stdev_count > 0
| addinfo
| rex mode=sed field=call_count "s/^/z_score_numerator=/"
| streamstats current=t window=1 values(call_count) as current_count
| where ((current_count - baseline_count) / stdev_count) > 3
| rename current_count as flagged_call_count
| table source_system, trunk_group, risk_country, _time, flagged_call_count,
        total_duration_sec, unique_callers, unique_destinations,
        avg_duration, baseline_count, stdev_count
| sort - flagged_call_count
queries.kql:
// KQL for IRSF Traffic Spike Detection
// Detects abnormal call volume to premium-rate international numbers
let premium_rate_calls = CallDetailRecords
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where CallDirection == "outbound"
| where DestinationType == "international"
| join kind=inner (PremiumRateRanges) on $left.DestinationPrefix == $right.NumberPrefix
| summarize CallCount = count(),
            TotalDurationSec = sum(CallDurationSeconds),
            UniqueCallers = dcount(CallingNumber),
            UniqueDestinations = dcount(CalledNumber),
            AvgDuration = avg(CallDurationSeconds)
  by SourceSystem, TrunkGroup, RiskCountry, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h);
let baselines = CallDetailRecords
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) and TimeGenerated < ago(1h)
| where CallDirection == "outbound"
| where DestinationType == "international"
| join kind=inner (PremiumRateRanges) on $left.DestinationPrefix == $right.NumberPrefix
| summarize HourlyCount = count()
  by SourceSystem, TrunkGroup, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| summarize BaselineCount = avg(HourlyCount), StdevCount = stdev(HourlyCount)
  by SourceSystem, TrunkGroup;
premium_rate_calls
| join kind=inner baselines on SourceSystem, TrunkGroup
| extend ZScore = iff(StdevCount > 0, (CallCount - BaselineCount) / StdevCount, 0.0)
| where ZScore > 3
| project SourceSystem, TrunkGroup, RiskCountry, TimeGenerated,
          CallCount, TotalDurationSec, UniqueCallers, UniqueDestinations,
          AvgDuration, BaselineCount, ZScore
| order by ZScore desc
queries.sql:
-- SQL for IRSF Traffic Spike Detection
-- Detects abnormal call volume to premium-rate international numbers using z-score
WITH hourly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    c.source_system,
    c.trunk_group,
    p.risk_country,
    DATE_TRUNC('hour', c.call_start_time) AS call_hour,
    COUNT(*) AS call_count,
    SUM(c.call_duration_seconds) AS total_duration_sec,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.calling_number) AS unique_callers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.called_number) AS unique_destinations,
    AVG(c.call_duration_seconds) AS avg_duration
  FROM call_detail_records c
  JOIN premium_rate_numbers p ON c.called_number LIKE p.number_prefix || '%'
  WHERE c.call_direction = 'outbound'
    AND c.destination_type = 'international'
    AND c.call_start_time >= DATEADD(HOUR, -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  GROUP BY c.source_system, c.trunk_group, p.risk_country,
           DATE_TRUNC('hour', c.call_start_time)
),
baselines AS (
  SELECT
    source_system,
    trunk_group,
    AVG(hourly_count) AS baseline_count,
    STDDEV(hourly_count) AS stdev_count
  FROM (
    SELECT source_system, trunk_group,
           DATE_TRUNC('hour', call_start_time) AS call_hour,
           COUNT(*) AS hourly_count
    FROM call_detail_records
    WHERE call_direction = 'outbound'
      AND destination_type = 'international'
      AND call_start_time >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
    GROUP BY source_system, trunk_group, DATE_TRUNC('hour', call_start_time)
  ) hist
  GROUP BY source_system, trunk_group
)
SELECT
  h.source_system,
  h.trunk_group,
  h.risk_country,
  h.call_hour,
  h.call_count,
  h.total_duration_sec,
  h.unique_callers,
  h.unique_destinations,
  h.avg_duration,
  b.baseline_count,
  CASE WHEN b.stdev_count > 0
       THEN (h.call_count - b.baseline_count) / b.stdev_count
       ELSE 0 END AS z_score
FROM hourly_stats h
JOIN baselines b ON h.source_system = b.source_system
                AND h.trunk_group = b.trunk_group
WHERE CASE WHEN b.stdev_count > 0
           THEN (h.call_count - b.baseline_count) / b.stdev_count
           ELSE 0 END > 3
ORDER BY z_score DESC

references: Subex, Global Telecom Fraud Intelligence Report (2025, 2026)
NDSS Symposium, ML-Based Detection of International Revenue Share Fraud
falsepositives: Legitimate international call campaigns (telemarketing, customer outreach) to premium-rate regions
Seasonal spikes in international calling (holidays, business cycles)
Network routing changes causing temporary traffic redistribution
Test calls during PBX maintenance or carrier migration
